raw_response:
I've been farming this same land for 20 years. The wheat-maize rotation is what everyone here does. My land is only 3.5 mu, so I can't afford mistakes, but I also can't afford to experiment. My kids and husband bring in money from off-farm work, so the farm doesn't have to carry the whole family, but I still need to produce well — we eat the grain and sell what's left.

**Wheat:** The wheat goes in every October on all 3.5 mu. I'll use the improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station for the past several years — it performs reliably here and I know how it behaves. I put down compound fertilizer as a base before seeding, then topdress urea at jointing. I'll irrigate three times: once before winter sets in, once at green-up in spring, and once at heading. Two to three rounds of chemicals — herbicide in autumn after emergence, then a fungicide spray in spring when powdery mildew shows up. I rotary till before seeding, same as always. I expect around 450 kg/mu.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June, I'll rotary till and get maize in quickly — can't waste days in this double-crop system. I use hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or Xianyu 335, whichever the village supply store has stocked. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and chase with urea at the big bell stage. Maize gets the summer rains but I'll irrigate twice — once around tasseling if it's dry, once at grain fill. Two pesticide passes: herbicide early and an insecticide if I see corn borer. I expect 550 kg/mu.
